Turn in, via GitHub, an updated draft data notebook (.RMD) that :
Loads and cleans the core data set to prepare for analysis. 

Shows basic exploratory analysis to demonstrate an understanding of the dataset, including the number of rows and columns, any obvious limitations or flaws and any reasons why it might not be able to answer the questions you've posed last week.

1. Some limitations to the data include, it only covers 2024. This may make it harder to compare different years, we will need to find more data. Also, this data is only showing precinct level data this could make it hard to answer questions that involve different districts, or jurisdictions, or zip codes. Lastly, questions about different voter demographics may be hard to answer, they are not included in the data. 

Task: Load libraries (we will probably want to load more libraries later to answer different questions)
```{r}
#load libraries 
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(lubridate) #could be helpful because we are working with dates
```

```{r}
#load data
md_precinct <- read_csv("MD 2024 General Precinct Results - md_election_results.csv") |> #clean names 
   clean_names()
```

```{r}
#check out different column and row numbers 
nrow(md_precinct) #there are 82772 rows 
ncol(md_precinct) #there are 14 columns 
```
